events.title: Coronal mass ejection (347 km/s)
events.summary: A cloud of solar plasma left the Sun at about 347 km/s, seen by coronagraphs from 09:09 UTC.

images.caption: NASA SDO/AIA 193 Å image of the whole Sun, 2026-09-21 09:07 UTC, 2 min before the reported time (09:09 UTC) of this coronal mass ejection. 193 Å shows the 1.5-million-°C corona, where an erupting CME leaves a dark dimming.
images.credit: Courtesy of NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams
images.license: Not copyrighted (NASA SDO image-use rules); credit line required

images.caption: SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph image, 2026-09-21 09:36 UTC, 28 min after the reported time (09:09 UTC) of this CME: the outer corona out to about 6 solar radii. The dark disk is the occulter blocking the bright Sun; a CME seen by LASCO shows as a bright cloud moving outward.
images.credit: SOHO/LASCO (ESA & NASA); rendered by Helioviewer.org
images.license: SOHO data are free to use with credit to SOHO (ESA & NASA)

events.title: C3.3 solar flare from active region 14535
events.summary: The Sun produced a small C3.3-class X-ray flare from active region 14535 at solar position N14E90, peaking at 18:17 UTC as measured by GOES.

images.caption: NASA SDO/AIA 131 Å image of the whole Sun, 2026-09-19 18:14 UTC, 2 min before the flare peak (18:17 UTC) of this flare. 131 Å shows plasma near 10 million °C, where flares glow brightest. The source reports the flare at N14E90 (NOAA active region 14535): on the left (east) edge of the disk, 14° north of the equator.
images.credit: Courtesy of NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE, and HMI science teams
images.license: Not copyrighted (NASA SDO image-use rules); credit line required

events.title: Gold high-energy neutrino (IceCube run 143143_38400235)
events.summary: The IceCube detector at the South Pole caught a high-energy neutrino (most likely about 303 TeV) coming from this part of the sky. IceCube estimates a 67% chance it came from space rather than Earth's atmosphere.

images.caption: DSS2 colour image of a 1° square of sky around this neutrino. Crosshair: the most likely position is at the centre, RA 111.04990°, Dec +6.42990°. Archival picture taken on photographic plates in the 1980s and 1990s: the stars and galaxies in the direction the neutrino came from. The true position lies within about 16.3′ of the centre.
images.credit: Digitized Sky Survey (STScI/NASA; POSS-II Caltech/Palomar, UK Schmidt AAO/ROE), colour HiPS by CDS; cut with CDS hips2fits
images.license: DSS plates © AURA, Caltech, AAO and UK PPARC; use with the STScI DSS acknowledgement; HiPS ODbL-1.0 (CDS)
